LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The `makepkg --printsrcinfo` command only executes the PKGBUILD's global/top-level scope. Examining the file, the top-level code consists of standard variable definitions (pkgname, pkgver, pkgrel, etc.) and a `source` variable assignment that contains only a string pointing to the GitHub tarball. There are no top-level command substitutions (e.g., `$(curl ...)`, `$(wget ...)`, `eval ...`), no global variable assignments that download or execute untrusted code, and no function calls to `pkgver()`, `prepare()`, `build()`, or `package()` at the top level. The `build()` and `package()` functions are defined but not executed during this step, so any potentially risky code inside them is not run. The provided SHA256 checksum is present (not SKIPped), which is standard practice. Since no malicious or dangerous operations are performed when sourcing/parsing this PKGBUILD, the command is safe.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>
<summary>Top-level PKGBUILD code contains only variable definitions and a source URL string; no command substitution or dangerous operations are present.</summary>

The dependencies listed (git, java-environment>=21, cargo, libxkbcommon, pkgconf, libappindicator, java-runtime>=21) are consistent with a Java/Rust-based desktop application. There is no obfuscated code, no network requests to unrelated hosts, no execution of downloaded content, and no unexpected system modifications. This file represents ordinary AUR packaging metadata.
